IMPLEMENTATION OF AGRISTACK AND DIGITAL AGRICULTURE MISSION

07 AUG 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

AgriStack is the farmer-centric Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) built as a public good for efficient, easier and faster service and scheme delivery to the farmers. It provides a comprehensive profile of every farmer, such as farmer’s details, land records, crops grown, and assets such as livestock and fisheries. It consists of three foundational registries associated with the agriculture sector, i.e., Farmer Registry, Geo-Referenced Village Maps and Crop Sown Registry, all created and maintained by the State Governments/ Union Territories. The Farmer Registry created under AgriStack is designed to serve as a foundational database for the efficient, transparent and faster delivery of agricultural services. Farmer Registry is being integrated with various farmer-centric schemes services and digital platforms to expedite credit disbursements, access to crop insurance, weather advisories, MSP-based crop procurement systems etc.

Farmer ID is created by synchronizing farmers' details with their digitized land records. As of 3rd August, 2026, more than 10.31 Crore Farmer IDs have been created across the country. Further, during Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was conducted in 648 Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the country. Manipur has initiated the process of DCS and participating in the process of creation of Farmer ID.

The State Farmer Registry is built in a federated manner, which means the ownership of the data is with the respective States. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has developed the AgriStack in accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025, to ensure the complete privacy of farmers' data by ensuring that farmers' data is collected only with their consent and farmers have full control over their data for sharing with authorized entities for specific purposes. Further, the security features of AgriStack are fully compliant with the cybersecurity guidelines of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In). AgriStack maintains farmers' information in an encrypted manner so that only the authorized systems can read it.

Under the YES-TECH initiative of the Crop Insurance Scheme, technology-based yield estimation is being implemented for Paddy, Wheat, and Soybean crops. Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning (ML) is one of the approach identified for crop yield estimation under this initiative.

For crop yield estimation, a digital initiative, Digital General Crop Estimation System (DGCES) has been developed, which provides accurate and timely crop yield data for crop production estimates.

The FPOs have been formed in different years since 2020-21 and are at different stages of development and business operations. Accordingly, their turnover varies, depending on the period of operation and the scale of business activities. The cumulative turnover reported by the FPOs formed under the Central Sector Scheme is ₹20,358 crore as on 31st July, 2026.

Implementaiton of National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)

07 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has approved the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with the objective of increasing the area and productivity of oil palm and thereby enhancing domestic production of edible oils and reducing dependence on imports. The Mission was launched in 2021-22 with a financial outlay of Rs. 11,040 crore, including a Government of India share of Rs. 8,844 crore, and a target of bringing 6.5 lakh hectares under oil palm cultivation during 2021-22 to 2025-26.

The Mission is being implemented in 15 States, (Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Karnataka, Kerala, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Tripura). The major interventions under NMEO-OP include assistance for planting material, maintenance of plantations, intercropping, drip irrigation, farm machinery, replanting, establishment of seed gardens and nurseries, and development of oil palm processing infrastructure, besides a price assurance mechanism for farmers through the Viability Gap Payment (VGP).

During 2021-22 to 2025-26, a total area of 2.73 lakh hectares was brought under oil palm cultivation. During the same period, Government of India released Rs. 1,447.21 crore to the implementing States under various components of the Mission.

The NMEO-OP was approved for the period 2021-22 to 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs. 11,040 crores. Subsequently, Annual Action Plans (AAPs) of 2026-27 for implementing states have been approved for Rs. 1143.9 crore.

In addition to NMEO-OP, the National Mission on Edible Oils – Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was launched on 3rd October, 2024 for seven years period from 2024-25 to 2030-31 to boost the domestic oilseed production and to strive toward self-sufficiency in edible oil. Under the mission, production of improved indigenous varieties and hybrids of oilseeds are being promoted through 100% support for purchase of breeder seeds and also promoted through distribution of certified seeds in the Value Chain Clusters. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seed of recently released varieties.

headline: STEPS TO INCREASE PRODUCTION OF OILSEEDS AND PULSES
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

STEPS TO INCREASE PRODUCTION OF OILSEEDS AND PULSES

07 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was approved on 3rd October, 2024 to boost domestic oilseed production and to strive towards self-reliance in edible oils. The mission aims to increase primary oilseed production from 39 million tonnes (2022-23) to 69.7 million tonnes by 2030-31.

The Government has launched the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses on 11th October, 2025 to increase the domestic production of pulses. The mission aims to increase pulse production from 242 lakh tonnes to 350 lakh tonnes by 2030-31.

The NMEO-OS is implemented through a cluster-based approach with market linkages. Over 600 Value Chain Clusters have been operationalized across the country which are managed by Value Chain Partners such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives and other agencies. Under these clusters, farmers are provided free high-quality seeds of latest high yielding varieties and training on good agricultural practices. The mission supports the establishment and upgradation of post-harvest infrastructure (oil mills) to improve oil recovery from primary and secondary sources. The mission focuses on improving the productivity through Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs), Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLDs) and Block-Level Demonstrations (BLDs) to help farmers to adopt latest high yielding varieties and good agricultural practices. The mission strengthens availability of certified seeds through 100% support for purchase of breeder seeds, establishment of new seed hubs and specialised seed storage units in the public sector to enhance production and storage capacity. Procurement of oilseeds from farmers also ensured at Minimum Support Price (MSP) through Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA).

Under the mission, 13.52 lakh hectares were covered under free seed distribution in Value Chain Clusters during 2025-26 and 4.44 lakh hectare area covered so far during kharif, 2026. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seeds of recently released varieties. Oilseeds production has increased from 413. 55 lakh tonnes in 2022-23 to 430.59 lakh tonnes in 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimate, DA&FW).

As reported by the Directorate of Sugar and Vegetable Oils, Department of Food and Public Distribution, the domestic availability of edible oils increased from 124.23 lakh tonnes in 2022–23 to 126.30 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 and edible oil imports declined from 165.00 lakh tonnes in 2022–23 to 160.72 lakh tonnes in 2024–25.

Under the Pulses Mission, assistance is provided to pulses farmers through State Governments/UTs on various interventions such as seed production, distribution of certified seeds of high yielding & climate resilient varieties and demonstration of latest crop production technologies, capacity building, seed kit distribution and strengthening post-harvest infrastructure. To ensure remunerative prices to farmers, the Mission supports assured procurement of Tur, Urad, Masoor from registered and willing farmers by National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF) under Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) based on requisitions made by the States.

During 2025-26, under the mission 4.79 lakh ha demonstrations were conducted on latest crop production & protection technologies, 4.33 lakh qtls of quality seeds were produced, 3.10 lakh qtls of certified seeds were distributed and 9.25 lakh seedkits were distributed free of cost to the farmers. The production of pulses has increased from 242.46 lakh tonnes during 2023-24 to 274.09 lakh tonnes during 2025-26 (3rd Advance estimate). Pulse imports declined from 72.56 lakh tonnes in 2024–25 to 59.64 lakh tonnes in 2025–26, reflecting improved domestic availability.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is implementing National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM) a Central Sector Scheme through National Bee Board (NBB).

The objectives of National Beekeeping and Honey Mission are to promote scientific beekeeping for holistic growth of beekeeping industry, increasing production of honey and beehive products, income & employment generation, providing livelihood support to farm and non-farm households, women empowerment through beekeeping, to strengthen beekeepers by developing institutional framework through collective approach and to enhance agriculture/ horticulture production. These include setting up of Integrated Beekeeping Development Centers, honey testing labs, bee disease diagnostic labs, Quality Nucleus Stock Development Centre, capacity building, technology demonstration, empowerment of women through beekeeping etc. NBHM also supports marketing, branding, value addition and Research & Development.

National Beekeeping and Honey Mission supplements the efforts of State Governments; Implementing Agencies and Stakeholder organizations to increase honey production, scientific beekeeping and enhancing agricultural productivity through project based approach, as per provisions of NBHM.

So far 7 world class honey testing labs, 66 mini labs to check adulteration, 83 honey processing units and 90 collection, branding & packaging units have been established. These support efficient storage and marketing. 81 Quality Nucleus Stock Development Centres have been supported for producing quality queen bees and colony multiplication so far. headline: HIGH ALTITUDE MEDICINAL PLANTS IN LADAKH
fullText:
HIGH ALTITUDE MEDICINAL PLANTS IN LADAKH

07 AUG 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

The government has taken cognizance of the fact that Ladakh possesses significant potential for the cultivation of high-altitude medicinal plants such as Seabuckthorn, Rhodiola, Artemisia and Aconitum. National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB) is implementing Central Sector Scheme (CSS) on “Conservation, Development and Sustainable Management of Medicinal Plants” throughout the country. The scheme is aimed at providing project based support for the different activities. The Forward and backward linkage in supply chain of medicinal plants (Integrated Component) is one of the component of CSS scheme wherein following activities are being supported:

Infrastructure for Quality Planting Material to raise the planting material of medicinal plants for cultivation.

Information Education Communication (IEC) activities to aware the farmers.

Infrastructure for Post-Harvest Management and Marketing to increase the marketability of the medicinal plants, adding value to the produce, increasing profitability and reducing losses.

Quality Testing and Certification of raw material.

NMPB has launched “e-CHARAK” mobile application as well as web portal for the promotion and marketing of medicinal plants/herbs. The “e-CHARAK” application supports different local languages and it also provides fortnightly market price of 100 MPs from 25 herbal markets across India including Ladakh.

NMPB facilitates market linkage to the farmers/ collectors involved in cultivation/collection of medicinal plants. The detailed requirements from major companies (along with contact details of person from purchase dept) is shared with all State Implementing Agencies and Regional-cum-Facilitation Centers supporting cultivation of Medicinal Plants.

Further, State Medicinal Plant Board (SMPB), Union Territory of Ladakh, has recognized the significant potential of high-altitude medicinal plants in the region due to its unique agro-climatic conditions and rich biodiversity. In this regard the SMPB, UT Ladakh conducts training programmes, seminars, workshops and buyer-seller meets to promote the scientific cultivation, conservation, and sustainable utilization of medicinal plants. In collaboration with concerned departments and research institutions, efforts are made to strengthen conservation, awareness and value addition.

The details of the projects sanctioned in Leh and Kargil under the National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB) during the last five years, indicating the funds sanctioned, released and utilized is placed at Annexure.

Ministry of Ayush is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National AYUSH Mission (NAM) through State/UT Governments including Leh and Kargil in Ladakh and providing financial assistance to them for overall development & promotion of Ayush systems of the medicine in the country against their proposals received through State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) as per the provisions of NAM guidelines. The Mission inter-alia makes provision for the following activities: -

Ayush Health & Wellness Centres now renamed as Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush) [AAM (Ayush)].

Co-location of Ayush facilities at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs) and District Hospitals (DHs).

Upgradation of existing standalone Government Ayush Hospitals.

Upgradation of existing Government/Panchayat/Government aided Ayush Dispensaries/Construction of building for existing Ayush Dispensary (Rented/ dilapidated accommodation)/Construction of building to establish new Ayush Dispensary in the area where there are no Ayush facilities available.

Setting up of upto 10/30/50 bedded Integrated Ayush Hospitals.

Supply of essential drugs to Government Ayush Hospitals, Government Dispensaries and Government/Government aided Teaching Institutional Ayush Hospitals.

Ayush Public Health Programmes.

Establishment of new Ayush colleges in the States where availability of Ayush teaching institutions is inadequate in Government Sector.

Infrastructural development of Ayush Under-Graduate Institutions and Ayush Post-Graduate Institutions/ add on PG/ Pharmacy /Para-Medical Course.

Further, as per the proposals received from UT Government of Ladakh through SAAPs, Ministry of Ayush has released an amount of Rs. 705.11 lakhs during last 05 years for implementation of different approved activities/projects of SAAPs and as reported they have utilized Rs. 534.24 lakhs. Further, there is no provision for release of district-wise funds under NAM.

SMPB, Union Territory of Ladakh has assessed the opportunities and constraints in the medicinal plant sector. Efforts are made through capacity-building programmes to address constraints and promote sustainable cultivation and commercialization of medicinal plants. Further, RCFC NR-II has consistently supported the establishment of post-harvest processing and quality-testing infrastructure in Ladakh for promoting sustainable cultivation and generating local employment.

Currently, NMPB Ministry of Ayush is implementing “Central Sector Scheme for Conservation, Development and Sustainable Management of Medicinal Plants” throughout the country. Under the scheme, the project-based support is provided for following activities:

Livelihood linkages with Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs) for value addition and livelihood generation in forest areas / Panchayats / Van Panchayats / Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) / Self Help Groups (SHGs).

Information Education and Communication (IEC) activities like Training / workshops / Seminars/ Conferences etc.

Research & Development.

Promotion of marketing and trade of medicinal plants produce.

Forward and backward linkage in supply chain of medicinal plants.

As per the information received from Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is implementing Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) for holistic development of horticulture throughout the country. Under MIDH, financial assistance is provided to the Public Sector only for for establishment of Center of Excellence (CoE).

A Centre of Excellence in Horticulture (CoE) is a specialized facility established with the objective of promoting excellence in horticultural practices, enhancing productivity, and ensuring sustainable development in the sector. These centers function as hubs of advanced research, demonstration, and training for farmers, entrepreneurs, and horticultural professionals. The CoE serves as demonstration and training centre for latest technologies in horticulture development. The centre also serves as source of planting material for fruits and vegetable seedlings for protected cultivation.

Under MIDH, a Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Seabuckthorn has been established at Nimoo, Leh with financial assistance of Rs. 789.33 lakh. The project was initiated during 2020-21 and implemented by the Department of Horticulture, UT Ladakh with technical support from Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) - Defence Institute of High-Altitude Research (DIHAR), Leh. The Centre comprises a scientific orchard, model nursery, demonstration and training facilities, primary processing unit and capacity-building programmes for farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), women and entrepreneurs.

The Centre promotes scientific cultivation, production of quality planting material, demonstration of primary processing technologies and capacity building of farmers, FPOs, SHGs, women and entrepreneurs. The Centre facilitates demonstration of pilot-scale processing, establishment of model orchards and nurseries, development of standard package of practices and knowledge transfer for strengthening the Seabuckthorn value chain.

headline: KERALA AS GLOBAL HUB FOR AYURVEDA TOURISM
fullText:
KERALA AS GLOBAL HUB FOR AYURVEDA TOURISM

07 AUG 2026 6:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has adopted a comprehensive strategy to promote Ayush-based tourism in the country. The Ministry of Tourism has formulated a National Strategy and Roadmap for Medical and Wellness Tourism in consultation with other Ministries including the Ministry of Ayush.

To facilitate international visitors seeking Ayush-based treatments, the Government introduced a separate category of Ayush Visa on 27 July 2023. Ministry of Ayush has also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC), Ministry of Tourism to work together for the promotion of Medical Value Travel (MVT) in Ayurveda and other traditional systems of medicine. So far, Ministry of Ayush has organized two Medical Value Travel Summits, one for Western zone on 30.09.2024 at Mumbai with participation of States/UTs of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Goa, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, and the other for the Southern Zone on 26.05.2025 at Chennai with participation of States/UTs like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Puducherry, with the aim of strengthening India’s position in Medical Value Travel.

The research activities in the State are undertaken through the units/institutes under the respective Research Councils of the Ministry of Ayush. At present, 34 research programmes are being carried out at the National Homoeopathy Research Institute in Mental Health (NHRIMH), Kottayam, which functions under the Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH). Two institutes under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) are functioning in the State of Kerala, namely the National Ayurveda Research Institute for Panchakarma (NARIP), Cheruthuruthy, and the Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Thiruvananthapuram. CCRAS has undertaken various research projects in the State, including Medico-Ethno Botanical Surveys (MEBS), ethno-dietary studies, inventory of phytodiversity of medicinal plants, and programmes related to the cultivation of medicinal plants. The Clinical Research Unit of the Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM) is functioning at Edathala, Kerala, and provides healthcare services across geriatric, reproductive, and non-communicable disease sectors. The Siddha Regional Research Institute (SRRI) functioning under the Central Council for Research in Siddha (CCRS), situated in Poojapura, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala is dedicated exclusively to research in Siddha medicine. The institute is actively involved in scientific validation of traditional Siddha formulations, evidence-based clinical studies, and standardization of Siddha medicines. This institute engages in Intramural Research (IMR) projects on clinical research, Drug Standardization Research and Medicinal Plants Research.

Under the National Ayush Mission (NAM), the Government of India extends financial assistance to the State of Kerala for strengthening Ayush healthcare services through the State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs), which are approved annually in accordance with the provisions of the NAM Operational Guidelines. The support provided under NAM includes both recurring and non-recurring grants. Recurring grants cover the supply of medicines and contingencies to Ayush institutions, as well as human resource support for Ayush hospitals. Non-recurring grants include infrastructure development such as construction, renovation, upgradation and strengthening of Ayush healthcare facilities, along with the provision of equipment and furniture for Ayush institutions.

Under the ‘Conservation, Development and Sustainable Management of Medicinal Plants’ a Central Sector Scheme implemented by National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), Ministry of Ayush, project based financial support is provided for research activities on various aspects of medicinal plants to government as well as private universities/research institutions/organizations across the country. The details are at Annexure I.

Under Ayurswasthya Yojana, a Central Sector Scheme, implemented by Ministry of Ayush, two Centres of Excellence (CoE) projects have been approved in Kerala. The details are at Annexure II.

The Government has taken the following steps to promote evidence-based Ayurveda, international accreditation, and exports of Ayurvedic products, including from Kerala:

To strengthen regulatory oversight, Ayush Vertical in Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) facilitates the issuance of the World Health Organization Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (WHO-CoPP) for eligible Ayush drugs through joint inspections with State/UT Licensing Authorities and CDSCO.

Ayush Standard Mark and Ayush Premium Mark are awarded to Ayush drugs by Quality Council of India (QCI) based on third-party assessment of compliance with prescribed national and international quality standards respectively. Ayush Quality Mark Programme was launched in 2025 by the Ministry of Ayush to strengthen quality assurance, enhance consumer confidence, and improve the global recognition and competitiveness of Ayush products and services. Over the years 77 Ayush healthcare organizations in Kerala are accredited by National Accreditation Board for Hospitals (NABH), a constituent board of the QCI.

Ayurveda and Yoga have been included under Sectional Committee 2 of ISO/TC249 to focus on international standards of Ayurveda and Yoga, terminology, quality and safety of ingredients, extracts, finished products, Ayurveda-based dietary supplements, Yoga accessories etc.

As reported by the Government of Kerala, a 14-member Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani (ASU) Standardization Committee has been constituted under the chairmanship of the Principal Secretary, Dept. of Ayush. The Committee has been tasked to examine the various challenges faced by the ASU drug manufacturing industry, to suggest practical solutions, and make recommendations for improving standardization across the sector. As part of its mandate, the Committee organized a one-day stakeholder workshop on 15 February 2024, bringing together representatives from the Ayurveda drug manufacturing industry and other relevant stakeholders. The workshop facilitated the identification of existing issues and explored feasible corrective measures for strengthening quality assurance and regulatory compliance.

headline: STANDARDIZATION OF AYUSH MEDICINES
fullText:
STANDARDIZATION OF AYUSH MEDICINES

07 AUG 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Ayush has taken following steps to promote the production, quality, standardization and export of Ayush medicines:

The Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs Rules, 1945 have exclusive regulatory provisions for Ayush drugs. It is mandatory for the manufacturers to adhere to the prescribed requirements for licensing of manufacturing units & medicines including proof of safety & effectiveness, compliance with the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) as per Schedule T and Schedule M-I of the Drugs Rules, 1945 for Ayurveda, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, Unani and Homeopathy drugs respectively and to follow the quality standards of drugs as prescribed in the respective pharmacopoeia.

Drug Inspectors collect medicine samples regularly from manufacturing firms or retail shops within their jurisdiction and send them to Drug Testing Laboratory under Drug Control department for quality testing and if any sample is found to be ‘Not of Standard Quality’, appropriate action is initiated to prevent the sale of such medicines in the market, along with legal proceedings as per the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder. There are 34 Drug Testing Laboratories available in State/UTs for testing of the Legal Samples drawn by the Drug Inspectors of concerned State/UTs.

The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), a subordinate organization under Ministry of Ayush, develops pharmacopoeial standards and formulary specifications for Ayush drugs, which serve as the official compendia for determining their identity, purity, and strength. Compliance with these standards is mandatory under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder. PCIM&H also functions as the Appellate Drug Testing Laboratory for Ayush drugs and conducts regular capacity-building programmes for Drug Regulatory Authorities, Drug Analysts, and other stakeholders on standardization, quality control, and testing methodologies to strengthen the quality assurance system for Ayush drugs.

Drug Testing Laboratories are approved by Ministry of Ayush under Rules 160A to 160J of the Drugs Rules, 1945, for carrying out tests relating to the identity, purity, quality and strength of Ayush drugs. As on date, 118 private Drug Testing Laboratories have been approved by Ministry across States and Union Territories for conducting such tests in accordance with the provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945.

Further, Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme, namely, Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) to support Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards like World Health Organization Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP) and National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) respectively.

In addition, Ministry of Ayush has undertaken the following initiatives to promote quality assurance and export of Ayush products:

World Health Organization Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (WHO-CoPP) is issued by Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) after joint inspection of manufacturing units by drug inspectors posted in Ayush Vertical in CDSCO along with drug inspectors of States/UTs and CDSCO for compliance with WHO Technical Report Series (TRS) guidelines for herbal medicines.

Ministry of Ayush has launched Ayush Quality Mark (AQM) initiative through the Ayush Export Promotion Council (AYUSHEXCIL). Under this framework, the Ayush Quality Mark is being granted after scrutiny and verification of valid quality certifications and statutory approvals issued by the competent Government authorities, such as WHO-GMP, Ayush Premium Mark and other recognised certifications, as applicable.

Ayush Standard Mark and Ayush Premium Mark are awarded to Ayush Drugs by Quality Council of India (QCI) based on third-party assessment of compliance with prescribed National and International quality standards.

Ayurveda and Yoga has been included under Sectional Committee 2 of ISO/TC249 to focus on International Standards of Ayurveda and Yoga terminology, quality and safety of ingredients, extracts, finished products, Ayurveda based dietary supplements, Yoga accessories etc.

The details of the total export value of Ayush and Herbal products and the major export destinations during the last five years, year-wise are at Annexure-I.

The Ministry of Ayush is implementing the Central Sector Scheme, namely Promotion of International Cooperation for Ayush to enhance the Global outreach of Ayush systems of medicine. The Scheme provides support to Indian Ayush drug manufacturers and Ayush service providers to promote the export of Ayush products and services. It also facilitates the International promotion, development, and recognition of Ayush systems of medicine; fosters engagement with International stakeholders and market development; promotes academic collaboration and research through the establishment of Ayush Academic Chairs in foreign countries; and supports the organization for conducting training programmes, workshops, and symposiums to strengthen Global awareness, understanding, and acceptance of Ayush systems of medicine.

Further, Ministry of Ayush has signed 27 Country to Country MoUs, 16 Ayush Chair MoUs and 57 Institute to Institute level MoUs for the International promotion and propagation of Ayush systems of medicine.

The Ministry of Ayush does not compile or maintain State-wise information relating to the production and export of Ayush medicines.

headline: AYUSH HEALTHCARE IN TRIBAL AREAS
fullText:
AYUSH HEALTHCARE IN TRIBAL AREAS

07 AUG 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi

Public Health being a State Subject, the primary responsibility to conduct assessment regarding the availability and accessibility of Ayush healthcare facilities, including Ayurvedic, Yoga, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy services in the country including rural and tribal areas, lies with respective State Government. However, Ministry of Ayush is regularly and vigorously monitoring the progress of implementation of various activities under National Ayush Mission (NAM) scheme through various methods as under: -

Collecting activity-wise physical/financial progress on regular interval from the State/UT Governments.

Conducting the field visits by central team of the Ministry of Ayush, time to time, to analyse the actual progress of implementation of different activities for which State Government has reported expenditure and submitted utilization certificates.

Regional Review Meetings with State/UTs under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister/Secretary to assess the implementation status and to decide way forward.

PROGRESS OF AYUSH HEALTHCARE SERVICES FOR WOMEN

07 AUG 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi

Public Health being a State Subject, the primary responsibility to review the progress of Ayush healthcare services for women in Tamil Nadu, particularly through the network of co-located Ayush units under the National Ayush Mission (NAM) in rural and coastal districts, lies with respective State Government. However, Ministry of Ayush is regularly and vigorously monitoring the progress of implementation of various activities under National Ayush Mission (NAM) scheme through various methods as under:-

Collecting activity-wise physical/financial progress on regular interval from the State/UT Governments.

Conducting the field visits by central team of the Ministry of Ayush, time to time, to analyse the actual progress of implementation of different activities for which State Government has reported expenditure and submitted utilization certificates.

Regional Review Meetings with State/UTs under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister/Secretary to assess the implementation status and to decide way forward.

One to one meeting with States/UTs conducted for detailed review of physical and financial progress.

Mid-term evaluation of NAM scheme implementation/progress by NITI Aayog through third party who undertakes field visits in State/UTs.

Further, State Government of Tamil Nadu reported that they regularly review the implementation and progress of Ayush healthcare services in Tamil Nadu under NAM. The performance of Ayush healthcare services is reviewed every month by the District Siddha Medical Officers at the district level and periodically at the State level. Under NAM, Ayush healthcare services for women are provided through a network of co-located Ayush units, Ayush Health & Wellness Centres [now known as Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush)], and Government Ayush institutions across the State, including rural and coastal districts. At present, 94 co-located Ayush units (Annexure-I) are functioning in rural districts under NAM Scheme, 40 in rural coastal districts (Annexure-II), and 16 in urban coastal districts under NAM (Annexure-III). During last year, a total of 1,11,02,499 beneficiaries availed Ayush healthcare services through various Ayush health facilities in Tamil Nadu under NAM Scheme. Women-specific healthcare services, including maternal healthcare, are provided through various Ayush interventions. Under the Siddha system of medicine, the Magaperu Sanjeevi Scheme provides medicine kits to pregnant women, under which 1,27,084 pregnant women benefited during the last year.

As reported by State Government of Tamil Nadu, a total of 3,47,112 women beneficiaries availed Ayush services relating to maternal and child health, anaemia management, adolescent health, menopause care and wellness during the last three years under the Magaperu Sanjeevi Scheme. The district-wise details of these women beneficiaries are enclosed as Annexure-IV.

Efforts are being made to further strengthen the integration of Ayush services with public healthcare institutions through digital health initiatives, including telemedicine and Health Management Information Systems (HMIS). Community outreach programmes, health awareness camps, yoga sessions, wellness activities and preventive healthcare initiatives are being conducted regularly through Ayush institutions and Health & Wellness Centres.

As reported by the State of Tamil Nadu, the Government is promoting preventive and holistic healthcare for women through AYUSH interventions across the State, including underserved districts. Regular Yoga and Naturopathy programmes for antenatal and postnatal care, lifestyle modification, stress management, nutrition counselling, mental well-being, and health awareness activities are being conducted through Government AYUSH institutions and AYUSH Health & Wellness Centres. During the last year, 1,31,160 women benefited from antenatal and postnatal Yoga and Naturopathy programmes. Further, awareness campaigns, yoga camps, wellness programmes and community-based preventive healthcare activities continue to be implemented to improve women's health and well-being.

INITIATIVES FOR PROMOTION OF AYUSH

07 AUG 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Ayush has launched several initiatives to promote the production, quality, research, marketing and Global acceptance of Ayush medicines. The major initiatives include:

Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY): Supports quality assurance, standardization, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), testing infrastructure, pharmacopoeial standards and capacity building of the Ayush drug sector.

AYURGYAN Scheme: Promotes evidence-based research, innovation, clinical studies and higher education in Ayush systems.

Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H): Development and publication of pharmacopoeial standards, formularies and quality standards for Ayush drugs.

International Cooperation Scheme (IC Scheme): Supports Indian Ayush drug Manufacturers/ Ayush Service providers to boost the export of Ayush products and services; facilitates the International promotion, development and recognition of Ayush systems of medicine; foster interaction of stakeholders and market development of Ayush at international level; promote academics and research through the establishment of Ayush Academic Chairs in foreign countries and holding training workshop/symposiums for promoting and strengthening awareness and interest about Ayush systems of Medicine at International level.

Ayush Export Promotion Council (Ayushexcil): Facilitates export of Ayush products and services by supporting exporters through International exhibitions, seminars, buyer-seller meets, and capacity building of manufacturers and service providers.

Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme, namely, Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) to support Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards like WHO Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP) and National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) respectively. The components of scheme are as follows: -

Strengthening and up-gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards.

Pharmacovigilance of ASU&H drugs including surveillance of misleading advertisements.

Strengthening of Central and State regulatory frameworks including Technical Human Resource & Capacity Building programs for Ayush drugs.

Support for development of standards and accreditation/certification of Ayush products & materials in collaboration with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Quality Control of India (QCI) and other relevant scientific institutions and industrial R&D centers.

The details of financial assistance provided to Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories including MSMEs during the last three years, State-wise including Karnataka is furnished at annexure-I.

Following steps have been taken by the Ministry to strengthen quality control, standardisation, pharmacovigilance and export of Ayush medicines-

The Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs Rules, 1945 have exclusive regulatory provisions for Ayush drugs. It is mandatory for the manufacturers to adhere to the prescribed requirements for licensing of manufacturing units & medicines including proof of safety & effectiveness, compliance with the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) as per Schedule T and Schedule M-I of the Drugs Rules, 1945 for Ayurvedic, Siddha, Sowa-rigpa, Unani and Homeopathy drugs respectively and to follow the quality standards of drugs as prescribed in the respective pharmacopoeia. Drug Testing Laboratories are approved by the Ministry of Ayush under Rules 160A to 160J of the Drugs Rules, 1945, for carrying out tests relating to the identity, purity, quality and strength of Ayush drugs. As on date, 118 private Drug Testing Laboratories have been approved by the Ministry across States and Union Territories for conducting such tests in accordance with the provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945.

Drug Inspectors collect medicine samples regularly from manufacturing firms or retail shops within their jurisdiction and send them to Drug Testing Laboratory under Drug Control department for quality testing and if any sample is found to be ‘Not of Standard Quality’, appropriate action is initiated such as preventing the sale of the medicines from the market and appropriate legal actions as per Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules made thereunder. There are 34 Drug Testing Laboratories available in State/UTs for testing of the Legal Samples drawn by the Drug Inspectors of concerned State/UTs.

The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), a subordinate organization under Ministry of Ayush, develops pharmacopoeial standards and formulary specifications for Ayush drugs, which serve as the official compendia for determining their identity, purity, and strength. Compliance with these standards is mandatory under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder. PCIM&H also functions as the Appellate Drug Testing Laboratory for Ayush drugs and conducts regular capacity-building programmes for Drug Regulatory Authorities, Drug Analysts, and other stakeholders on standardization, quality control, and testing methodologies to strengthen the quality assurance system for Ayush drugs.

The Pharmacovigilance Program for Ayush drugs under AOGUSY scheme functions through a nationwide three-tier network comprising 01 National Pharmacovigilance Co-ordination Centre (NPvCC), 05 Intermediary Pharmacovigilance Centres (IPvCs), and 97 Peripheral Pharmacovigilance Centres (PPvCs) established across the country. These centres are mandated to monitor suspected adverse drug reactions and report the misleading advertisements to the respective State Regulatory Authorities for suitable action against the defaulter(s). Further, through this program various stakeholders across the country are sensitised towards the quality of medicines, posologies and other drug-related issues. To strengthen the pharmacovigilance system for Ayush drugs, Ministry of Ayush has launched an IT enabled online portal “Ayush Suraksha” on 30th May 2025 to capture MLAs/OAs and report suspected Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) related to the Ayush medicine.

Further, Ministry of Ayush has undertaken the following initiatives to promote quality assurance and certification of Ayush products in order to promote export of Ayush medicines.

WHO Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (WHO-CoPP) to Ayush drugs is issued by Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) after joint inspections of manufacturing units by Drug Inspectors posted in Ayush vertical along with drug inspectors of State/UTs and CDSCO for compliance with WHO Technical Report Series (TRS) guidelines for Herbal Medicines.

Ministry of Ayush has launched Ayush Quality Mark (AQM) initiative through the Ayush Export Promotion Council (AYUSHEXCIL). Under this framework, the Ayush Quality Mark is being granted after scrutiny and verification of valid quality certifications and statutory approvals issued by the competent Government authorities, such as WHO-GMP, Ayush Premium Mark and other recognised certifications, as applicable.

The Ministry of Ayush has taken the following measures to increase the availability of certified Ayush medicines and public awareness across the country;

Under centrally sponsored scheme of National Ayush Mission, State/UT Governments are being supported for supply of essentials Ayush medicines for Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) and Government Ayush hospitals/dispensaries as per the proposal received in their State Annual Action Plan (SAAP).

The Ayush Export Promotion Council (AYUSHEXCIL), notified by Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Ministry of Commerce and supported by Ministry of Ayush, has signed Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with quick-commerce platform Zepto on January 28, 2026, and the Spice Board of India on May 25, 2026, to promote digital domestic delivery and boosting International exports of Ayush Medicines respectively.

Public awareness initiatives through Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns, observance of International Day of Yoga, Ayurveda Day, Social Media campaign and other outreach programmes like national and international exhibitions, fairs and conferences etc.

headline: 12th Session of India-Russia Working Group on Modernization & Industrial Cooperation Held in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

12th Session of India-Russia Working Group on Modernization & Industrial Cooperation Held in New Delhi

Talks Highlight Deepening Bilateral Cooperation in Vande Bharat project, Rail Infrastructure, SJ-100 Aircraft, Critical Minerals, and UAVs

07 AUG 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

The 12th Session of the India-Russia Working Group on Modernization and Industrial Cooperation under the Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation was held on August 7, 2026, at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi.

Shri Amardeep Singh Bhatia, Secretary, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, co-chaired from the Indian side, while H.E. Mr. Alexey Gruzdev, Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade of Russia, co-chaired from the Russian side.

The meeting reviewed progress since the 11th session and discussed collaboration across the identified sub-groups on modernization, mining, fertilizers and railway transport. Key areas in the 12th Session included cooperation in the field of modern industrialisation, science and technology, aerospace, railway infrastructure, mineral fertilizers and chemicals, rare earths and critical minerals, exploration and capacity building in REs, power engineering, industrial infrastructure, mining equipments, aluminium sector and joint venture for urea production, etc.

New areas of cooperation in railway transport such as infrastructure facilities, Vande Bharat train project, and signalling equipment were welcomed. Moreover, cooperation in Unmanned Aerial systems (UAVs), 3-D printing, production of Russian regional aircraft SJ-100, and aero-engine were also discussed. Further, cooperation in carbon-fibre technologies and propulsion systems, DAP/NPK fertilizer supplies, automation, critical minerals, lithium mining and titanium technologies, along with enhanced collaboration in aluminium, mining equipments and exploration of rare earth elements were discussed during the session.

The Protocol of the 12th Session of the Working Group was signed by both the co-chairs reaffirming the strategic India-Russia partnership with the aim to deepen industrial and economic cooperation. The session was attended by around 60 delegates from both sides.

headline: A high-level bilateral meeting on Co-operation on Trans-border Rivers held between Royal Government of Bhutan and Ministry of Jal Shakti in New Delhi

Ministry of Jal Shakti

A high-level bilateral meeting on Co-operation on Trans-border Rivers held between Royal Government of Bhutan and Ministry of Jal Shakti in New Delhi

07 AUG 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level bilateral meeting on Co-operation on Trans-border Rivers was held today in New Delhi between the delegation from the Royal Government of Bhutan, led by Lyonpo Gem Tshering, Minister for Energy & Natural Resources, and the delegation from the Government of India, led by Shri C R Paatil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti.

During the bilateral meeting, the two sides reviewed the ongoing cooperation between India and Bhutan in the water resources sector, with particular focus on trans-border river management, flood forecasting and flood management, hydrological data sharing, and other areas of mutual interest. The Ministers also reviewed the progress of the Punatsangchhu-I Hydroelectric Project, which is being implemented in Bhutan in partnership with the Government of India, and discussed measures for its expeditious implementation.

The two delegations held constructive discussions on proposals for the upgradation and strengthening of the existing hydro-meteorological network in Bhutan and the enhancement of the scope of cooperation of the existing mechanism for sharing hydrological data on trans-border rivers.

Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to sustainable and mutually beneficial management of trans-boundary water resources and agreed to further deepening of bilateral cooperation in the field of water resources through sustained technical collaboration, mutual trust, and regular institutional engagement.

headline: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, in association with TRIFED, showcases India’s Rich Tribal Textile Heritage through RISA: TIMELESS TRIBAL on the occasion of 12th National Handloom Day
fullText:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs

Ministry of Tribal Affairs, in association with TRIFED, showcases India’s Rich Tribal Textile Heritage through RISA: TIMELESS TRIBAL on the occasion of 12th National Handloom Day

Celebrating the Tribal Weaves of India

07 AUG 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, and Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Ltd. (TRIFED), organized “Tribal Weaves of India” at the RISA Flagship Store, State Emporia Complex, Baba Kharak Singh Marg, New Delhi, to mark the 12th National Handloom Day on 7th August 2026. The event showcased the rich diversity of India’s tribal textile traditions through RISA: Timeless Tribal.

The event was inaugurated by Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs (STA). In her address, she emphasised the importance of creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for tribal communities through stronger market linkages, enabling them to establish a distinct presence in the niche textile segment and meet the evolving aspirations of a wider clientele. She further highlighted that tribal textiles embody generations of indigenous knowledge, cultural identity and sustainable practices, and reiterated that initiatives such as RISA provide an important platform for preserving these traditions while expanding market access and creating enhanced livelihood opportunities for tribal artisans across the country.

Addressing the gathering, Shri M. Rajamurugan, Managing Director, TRIFED, stated that RISA: Timeless Tribal is a premium brand launched by Ministry of Tribal Affairs, that operates under TRIFED, with the vision of preserving India's tribal weaving and craft traditions while connecting them with discerning consumers in India and across the world. He further stated that the brand seeks to position tribal textiles and handicrafts as premium offerings by combining authenticity, quality and contemporary design, while creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for tribal artisans and expanding their access to national and international markets.

The inauguration was followed by a panel discussion on “What Makes Tribal Weaves Timeless?” which brought together eminent personalities from the fields of academia, textiles, design and crafts.

The session was moderated by Smt. Asha Baxi, Founding Faculty and former Dean, National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT). The distinguished panel comprised Smt. Jaya Jaitly, renowned craft revivalist and Founder of Dastkari Haat Samiti, Shri Gaurav Jai Gupta, Founder and Creative Director of Akaaro, Shri Gaurang Shah, Textile Artist, Shri Ramesh Menon, Founder of Save the Loom and Ms. Anju Modi, Fashion Designer.

The panel deliberated on ways of preserving traditional knowledge while creating contemporary design and market opportunities for tribal artisans. They explored the enduring relevance of India's tribal weaving traditions, the preservation of rich knowledge systems, contemporary design interventions and sustainable market linkages for tribal textiles. The discussion also emphasised the importance of fostering collaboration among artisans, designers, institutions and industry stakeholders to ensure that tribal weaving traditions continue to thrive while retaining their authenticity and cultural significance in an evolving global marketplace.

The event featured a collection of exquisite GI-tagged weaves, including Kotpad Cotton, Tussar Silk, Eri Silk, Muga Silk, Toda embroidery and Dongria embroidery from different states, along with collections by leading Indian fashion designers including Shri Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla, Ms. Anju Modi, Shri Manish Tripathi, Shri Gaurav Jai Gupta and Ms. Sameera Dalvi featuring textiles sourced directly from tribal weavers. RISA also showcased specialized handicrafts, including Longpi Pottery (Manipur), Turtuk Brass Cutlery (Ladakh), Warli Art (Maharashtra), and the world-renowned Dokhra Art (Chhattisgarh).

The event also included the felicitation of Tribal Master Artisans, a curated walkthrough of exquisite tribal textiles, and live demonstrations of Warli and Gond art on tribal textiles, offering visitors an opportunity to experience India's rich tribal artistic and textile heritage.

The event successfully raised awareness of RISA and reinforced its unique positioning as an artisan- and craft-led brand, rather than just another fashion label. At the heart of the brand lies its unique value proposition: celebrating traditions deeply rooted in India's history, culture, and social customs. These traditions embody a rich repository of India's cultural heritage and indigenous knowledge that must be preserved and cherished for all time to come.

Beyond aesthetics, RISA serves a vital socio-economic purpose by creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for tribal artisans. With the launch of RISA and through initiatives such as "Tribal Weaves of India", the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and TRIFED reaffirmed their commitment, in line with the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister, for the holistic socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes, with a strong focus on promoting tribal crafts, textiles, and indigenous knowledge systems.

headline: Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya calls for transparent selections, athlete-centric governance and institutional reforms at National Sports Federation Conclave 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya calls for transparent selections, athlete-centric governance and institutional reforms at National Sports Federation Conclave 2026

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasised the need to keep athletes on the playing field and build a strong league culture in the country,” says Dr. Mandaviya

“No injustice should ever be meted out to any athlete,”: Dr. Mandaviya

07 AUG 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya today chaired the National Sports Federation (NSF) Conclave 2026, attended by Ministers of State for Youth Affairs & Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse, senior officials of the Ministry, the Sports Authority of India (SAI), and representatives of National Sports Federations (NSFs).

The conclave focused on strengthening sports governance, enhancing athlete welfare, and reviewing India’s preparedness for upcoming major international sporting events.

The conclave featured detailed presentations on compliance status of National Sports Federations under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, good governance practices in sports bodies, and the preparedness of NSFs for the Asian Games 2026, Los Angeles Olympics 2028 and the Commonwealth Games 2030.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya emphasised that the interests and welfare of athletes must remain the foremost priority for every stakeholder in the sporting ecosystem.

“It is our responsibility to ensure that no athlete is ever subjected to injustice. Injustice can take many forms, and wherever such a situation arises,” he said.

Calling for complete transparency in athlete selection processes, the Union Minister said that selection trials must be conducted in a fair and accountable manner.

“Open selection trials should be recorded on camera in the presence of observers. There should be absolutely no compromise on transparency in the selection process,” Dr. Mandaviya stated.

Highlighting the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for Indian sports, Dr. Mandaviya said, “The Prime Minister has consistently emphasised the need to keep athletes on the playing field and develop a strong league culture in the country. Every National Sports Federation must work towards creating greater competitive opportunities for athletes throughout the year.”

The Union Minister also underscored the need for a comprehensive strategy to eliminate doping from Indian sports. Stressing that the existing framework requires strengthening, he said the Government is working on amendments to make the anti-doping ecosystem more effective.

“We must collectively tackle the menace of doping. It is not enough to act only against athletes. The entire chain—from manufacturers and suppliers to facilitators and users—must be identified and dealt with through a transparent and robust mechanism. Only then can we effectively eradicate doping from sports,” he said.

Dr. Mandaviya further stressed the importance of developing a strong indigenous coaching ecosystem and reducing overdependence on foreign coaches.

“We need to build a repository of quality Indian coaches. Along with training athletes, we must invest equally in training our coaches by providing them the best opportunities and international exposure. A well-trained coach will ultimately create world-class athletes for the country,” he said.

The Union Sports Minister reaffirmed Modi Government’s commitment to working closely with National Sports Federations to strengthen governance standards, ensure compliance with the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, and enhance India’s preparations for the Asian Games 2026, Los Angeles Olympics 2028 and the Commonwealth Games 2030.

(Release ID: 2296149)
